title: Central simple algebras and continuous Galois degree-two classes
statement: For every field K, its set of Brauer equivalence classes of finite-dimensional central simple K-algebras is in bijection with H²_G(Ks^×) [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology].

source.place: Theorem 03R7, its scalar-defect construction following Lemma 03R6, and Section 0DVG

proof.text: A central simple algebra splits over a finite Galois extension. Its projective-linear descent cocycle lifts to matrices whose scalar defects give a continuous two-cocycle. Changes of lifts give coboundaries; tensor products multiply the scalar defects, and matrix amplification preserves the class. Thus this construction is well-defined on Brauer equivalence.

When the scalar defect is a coboundary, adjust the lifts to a general-linear cocycle. Matrix Hilbert 90 trivializes that cocycle and descends a vector space V with algebra End_K(V). Thus the kernel consists of split algebras. Applying this to A tensor B^op proves injectivity.

A continuous class is represented over a finite Galois extension L/K. The twisted algebra with L-basis u_g and relations u_g a=g(a)u_g and u_g u_h=c(g,h)u_gh is central simple and realizes the class (up to the chosen scalar-defect sign convention). Hence the map is surjective. Homogeneous and inhomogeneous continuous cochains are identified by their usual change of variables, giving the indicated bijection. Since G is compact Hausdorff, the compact-open exponential law identifies Mathlib iterated continuous maps with continuous maps on finite powers of G. TopModuleCat homology has underlying algebraic kernel modulo image, so forgetting its topology preserves the cocycle classes.
